Anarthrous substantival adjective expanded as *a man sick of the palsy*. The supplied *a man* is the generic completion and is excluded by rule 17's anarthrous clause; within the adjective's own English, rule 66 puts the head on *palsy*, the word that glosses παραλυτ-, and not on the formal English head *sick*, which carries no part of the lexeme. Rule 66's own clause on `πιθανολογίᾳ` → *persuasiveness of speech* heading on *speech* is the shape: English syntax may make the modifier the phrase's formal head and put the meaning-bearing word in a complement. Heading on *sick* remains defensible but rests only on that syntax, which rule 17 forbids.

review_notes: Corrected: both παραλυτικός units now head on *palsy* rather than *sick*. Rule 66's compound clause is explicit that the core word takes the head even where English syntax makes the modifier the formal head and puts the core in a complement (*persuasiveness of speech* on *speech*), and *sick* glosses no part of παραλυτ-.
Edges are unchanged throughout; only the two target heads moved.
